parts.name: Soleus contribution

J Bone Joint Surg Am 89(4):758-764 -- the correct source (corrected from an earlier draft's citation of a different, same-year LaPrade paper on the knee's MEDIAL part, JBJS Am 89(9):2000-2010, which does not describe semimembranosus's distal expansions -- caught by adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md). This paper's abstract states verbatim that the semimembranosus tendon has 8 attachments distal to the main common tendon, with the main components being a lateral expansion to the oblique popliteal ligament, a direct arm to the tibia, an anterior arm, and a distal tibial expansion forming a posterior fascial layer over popliteus -- matching the 4 parts modeled here.

function: One of the most structurally complex distal tendon insertions in the body -- rather than one simple bone attachment, semimembranosus fans into several distinct fibrous expansions (this dataset models 4 of the more consistently documented ones; some sources describe up to 5), giving it an outsized dynamic stabilizing role for the posteromedial knee corner beyond simple knee flexion.

parts.name: Iliopsoas tendon
parts.function_note: Psoas major (via the lumbar plexus/vertebrae) and iliacus (via the iliac fossa) converge onto one shared distal tendon at the lesser trochanter -- a snapping/catching sensation of this tendon over the iliopectineal eminence or femoral head is a recognized cause of 'internal' snapping hip syndrome.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The shared distal tendon of psoas major and iliacus, two muscles with entirely separate proximal origins (vertebral column vs. iliac fossa) that functionally act as one combined hip flexor via this single conjoined insertion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

parts.name: Adductor magnus distal tendon
parts.function_note: The adductor part's tendon inserts on the adductor tubercle, leaving a gap in the muscle's distal attachment -- the adductor hiatus -- through which the femoral vessels pass from the anterior thigh (adductor/subsartorial canal) into the popliteal fossa, becoming the popliteal vessels; a key anatomical landmark for vascular surgical access to the distal femoral/popliteal arteries.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The distal tendon of adductor magnus's adductor part, notable less for its own structure than for the vascular hiatus its insertion pattern creates.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
